narrative.overview: Conversation and audio control take precedence over visual effects.
keyCharacteristics: A deep rail separates navigation from the conversation workspace.
Lilac identifies primary actions, selected navigation and keyboard focus.
Shared forms make TTS, RVC and model downloads feel part of the same application.

rules.name: The layout explains, not the text (#614)
rules.body: What a part of the screen is, what it belongs to and what state it is in are shown by where it sits and by its shape, size, color and motion. A secondary label or a line of explanation is added only where the layout cannot carry the meaning. A longer explanation is not kept on screen: it goes in a tooltip that opens on mouse-over (and on keyboard focus), and its words stay in the control's accessible name or description. This takes away no word that carries a meaning: a control keeps its name, a readout still states its condition in words, consent stays visible, and color never says something alone. New screens, the information architecture (#554) and the components (#452) start from this principle. Rules below that predate it, such as the visible first sentence of a general description, stay until the screens are reviewed against it.

dos: Do preserve model consent, dirty-form guards, independent switches and stop/mute behavior.
Do check Japanese labels, long paths, keyboard navigation and narrow windows using production components.
Do retain the distinction between configured, pending, active and failed states.
donts: Don't introduce remote fonts or a new UI framework for this redesign.
Don't imply connection, model readiness or microphone activity through decorative indicators.
